..
Issued at 1257 PM CDT Mon Oct 19 2026

Quiet conditions continue across the region with current temps in 
the lower to mid 60s and winds out of the east/southeast. The high 
pressure system that was over the region earlier this morning has 
tracked east/northeast with the center of the high over the Great 
Lakes Region and southern Ontario. Through tonight the region sits 
between this high to our east and an area of low pressure to our 
west as winds at the surface become more southeasterly late tonight 
with locations east of the Rockies under a broad upper level ridge 
per cutoff closed low over the northern Pacific which will track 
south/southeast and near the southern CA coast by Wednesday morning.

A weak shortwave will traverse eastward across Canada Tuesday and 
Wednesday with a secondary low developing along the front over 
western SD Tuesday and tracking across SD on the front before 
weakening. With this ongoing dry air mass, no precipitation is 
expected with this fropa passage as it tracks west to east across 
the CWA with the only indicator is winds will switch from the 
south/southeast to the north/northeast Wednesday morning and turning 
more easterly by Wednesday evening as a high continues to track 
along the northern CONUS/Canada border. A ridge then amplifies aloft 
over the central CONUS Wednesday evening and Thursday with 
surface/850mb winds switching out of the south really bringing in 
the WAA and a bit of low level moisture as dewpoints are forecast to 
rise back into the 50s through Friday ahead of the low within the 
warm sector. With diurnal heating and mixing, highs are forecast to 
range in the 70s to potentially the lower 80s, warmest over south 
central SD both Thursday and Friday. We may be flirting with record 
warm highs Friday morning per stronger WAA winds at 850mb to sfc. 
Probability of temps>80 per NBM is 30-50% Thursday afternoon and 40-
65% Friday over south central SD which leads to higher confidence on 
the warmer day being Friday as much of the region will be south of 
the warm front by peak heating. However, NBM 25-75th spread is about 
3-5 degrees Thursday and 5-7 degrees on Friday so there could still 
be some wiggle room on temps as we are still a few days away.  

Clusters agree on this cutoff low moving onshore over the southern 
CA coast ~late Wednesday night/early Thursday morning and becoming a 
negative tilted open wave with a shortwave moving in over western 
Canada. The northern wave will track east and the southern wave 
northeast and somewhat phasing together over the western CONUS 
Friday with the entire trough continuing its track northeast. 
Otherwise as mentioned, its low will develop and deepen 
(~1000mb)over the northern Rockies Friday and track northeast into 
Canada as the fropa tracks across the region with the CWA behind the 
system by Saturday evening. This will bring the return of 
precipitation, in the form of rain, starting with spotty chances (15-
25%) Friday (mainly over northeastern SD/MN associated with the warm 
front, with the bulk of the precip (NBM 30-50%) ahead and along the 
front as it tracks east/northeast across the CWA through Saturday 
morning. Not too much in the form of QPF with a probability of 24hr 
QPF>0.10" ending 00Z Sunday per NBM is 20-45% along and east of a 
line from Pierre to Aberdeen highest across east SD into MN. This is 
fairly close to what the grand ensemble (GEFS/ENS/GEPS) is 
forecasting. Low confidence in exact track and of the system along 
with estimated rainfall amounts at this time. 

Thursday and Friday will also be windy too as pressure gradients 
steepen across the region combining with gustier winds aloft behind 
the exiting high and low pressure to our west with gusts between 30-
40 mph across central SD Thursday afternoon and 30-45 mph Friday 
afternoon. Probability of wind gusts>45 mph is up to 45-55% over 
portions of the southern CWA and along the James Valley. With gusty 
winds and warm temps the end of the week will lead to elevated fire 
weather concerns across central SD Thursday and the entire CWA 
Friday even as forecast min RH will stay above 40%.
